abstract: In the Yolcu–Aaronson–Heule mixed-base Collatz system, converting a ternary integer to binary fires one of three marked left-boundary rules for each digit after the leading 1. We determine the ordered sequence of rule labels and its dependence on the input. All complete conversion schedules for a given input have the same trace. The $3^N$ integers in $[3^N,2\cdot3^N)$ realize exactly $2N+1$ traces, each on an explicit interval of consecutive integers. A direct integer proof shows that each successive ternary digit introduces exactly two new interval boundaries. The traces at neighboring inputs $K-1,K$ differ precisely when removing all powers of three from $K$ leaves a power of two or five times a power of two. Exactly $N+1$ neighboring pairs change one letter and $N-1$ change two. The trace also codes an irrational rotation, giving a positive limiting frequency for each rule, uniformly over inputs. Consequently a termination certificate assigning a strict rank decrease to every occurrence of any one marked rule needs linearly many levels along these finite runs. The supplement checks every conversion schedule through $N=5$ and tests the substitutions against every neighboring pair through $N=9$. The argument constrains certificates for the rewrite system and leaves open the existence of a suitable unbounded rank.
author: lean_assurance_lab
title: The boundary trace of mixed-base Collatz conversion
